To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

A series of novel indolin-2-onesulfonamides were synthesized and tested for their inhibitory activities against the human (h) isoforms I, IV, II and VII of the zinc metalloenzyme carbonic anhydrae (CA, EC 6.3.5.1) and their inhibition potencies have been rationalized by means of molecular docking studies.

novel sulfonamido-indolinones were designed, synthesized and evaluated as inhibitors of hCA isoforms I, IV and VII, and the most potent compounds were found to be those bearing a (4-oxo-thiazolidin-3-ylidene)-aminoethyl linker.

(i) the synthesized compounds 3a-f, as well as 9a-f, are the most potent inhibitors of hCA II, IV, and VII, with Ki values in the low nanomolar range, and (ii) the synthesized compounds are the first reported inhibitors of hCA VII, with Ki in the low nanomal range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of novel sulfonamide derivatives as hCAs inhibitors.

the design, synthesis and evaluation of novel sulfonamide derivatives incorporating substituted indolinones as tails, as well as with the evaluation of these compounds for their ability to inhibit four different human carbonic anhydrasae (hCA) isoforms (I, II, IV, and VII).
the design and synthesis of new indolin-2-onesulfonamides as hCA I, hCA II, hCA IV, and hCA VII inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the indolin-2-ones-based sulfonamidic derivatives are a promising class of CAIs, with the potential to be used for the development of novel therapeutic drugs.
all tested compounds were found to be effective hCA I, hCA II, hCA IV and hCA VII inhibitors, with some of the compounds being very selective for one of these isoforms.
the tested sulfonamides are potent inhibitors of hCA I, hCA II, hCA IV and hCA VII, with some compounds being more potent than the clinically used drug acetazolamide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the indolin-2-ones-based sulfonamiders reported herein represent a novel class of CAIs with potential for the treatment of glaucoma, edemas, and other pathologies linked to hCA II overexpression.

the sulfonamido-indolin-2-one derivatives reported here are potent inhibitors of the four hCAs isoforms tested and that the presence of a thiazolidine-2,4-dione moiety in the molecule, as in the case of compounds 3b, 3e and 6b, leads to an increased inhibition potency against all the tested isoforms.
the synthesized sulfonamiders 3a-f and 6a-f, bearing aminoethyl linkers, are more potent inhibitors than 9a-f, which bear (4-oxo-thiazolidin- 2-ylidenediaminoethyl) linkers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the indolin-2-ones can be considered as a new scaffold in the design of CA inhibitors, which could be further exploited for drug development.
the presence of the tail (indolin-2-one moiety) in these sulfonamides is not essential for the inhibition of these hCA isozymes.
the presence of the tail moiety in the tested sulfonamides has an influence on their inhibition activity, as well as their linker length.
